"""MockLLM: the deterministic stand-in for the LLM that LPR queries.

*LPR: Large Language Models-Aided Program Reduction* asks a model for rewrites a
syntax-guided reducer cannot express.  Perses can only delete or replace
subtrees, so it never turns ``helper(5)`` into ``5 * 2`` and never collapses a
loop into its iterations; an LLM does that happily because it understands what
the code *means*.

Talking to a real model would make the benchmark non-deterministic and require
network access, so this module answers the very same prompts with regex-driven
rewrites.  The five transformation types are the ones LPR uses:

===========================  ====================================================
``function_inlining``        replace calls of a one-line function by its body
``loop_unrolling``           replace a bounded loop by its iterations
``variable_elimination``     propagate an assignment into its uses
``data_type_elimination``    drop class/type definitions nobody references
``data_type_simplification`` collapse containers into a simpler shape
===========================  ====================================================

Every rewrite is only a *proposal*: exactly like a real LLM the mock may return
a program that no longer triggers the bug, which is why
:mod:`reduction.lpr.llm_reducer` validates each answer with the property tester
and throws it away when it does not hold up.

:meth:`MockLLM.transform` reports both the cumulative rewrite (every opportunity
of that kind applied) and the individual single-edit candidates, so a caller can
fall back to smaller steps when the big rewrite breaks the program.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

from reduction.token import KEYWORDS

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Transformation names
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
FUNCTION_INLINING = "function_inlining"
LOOP_UNROLLING = "loop_unrolling"
VARIABLE_ELIMINATION = "variable_elimination"
DATA_TYPE_ELIMINATION = "data_type_elimination"
DATA_TYPE_SIMPLIFICATION = "data_type_simplification"

#: The five transformation types, in the order LPR applies them.
TRANSFORMATIONS: Tuple[str, ...] = (
    FUNCTION_INLINING,
    LOOP_UNROLLING,
    VARIABLE_ELIMINATION,
    DATA_TYPE_ELIMINATION,
    DATA_TYPE_SIMPLIFICATION,
)

#: Instruction sent with each prompt; part of the mock's "API surface".
INSTRUCTIONS: Dict[str, str] = {
    FUNCTION_INLINING:
        "Inline every function whose body is a single return statement into "
        "its call sites and delete the definition.",
    LOOP_UNROLLING:
        "Unroll loops with a statically known, small iteration count into the "
        "individual iterations.",
    VARIABLE_ELIMINATION:
        "Replace variables that are assigned once by their value and delete "
        "the assignment.",
    DATA_TYPE_ELIMINATION:
        "Delete class and type definitions that nothing else references.",
    DATA_TYPE_SIMPLIFICATION:
        "Simplify composite data structures (dicts, lists, comprehensions) to "
        "the simplest shape that keeps the program meaningful.",
}

SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "You are helping to reduce a program while keeping the behaviour of "
    "interest. Answer with the rewritten program only."
)

#: Names that must not be treated as ordinary variables.
RESERVED = frozenset(KEYWORDS) | frozenset({
    'self', 'cls', 'print', 'len', 'sum', 'range', 'int', 'str', 'float',
    'list', 'dict', 'set', 'tuple', 'bool', 'sorted', 'max', 'min', 'abs',
    'open', 'type', 'enumerate', 'zip', 'map', 'filter',
})

DEFAULT_MAX_UNROLL = 4
DEFAULT_MAX_EDITS = 32
DEFAULT_MAX_CANDIDATES = 8


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Regexes
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#: A string literal; used to keep rewrites out of string contents.
STRING_RE = re.compile(
    r'("""(?:.|\n)*?"""'
    r"|'''(?:.|\n)*?'''"
    r'|"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"'
    r"|'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*')"
)

DEF_RE = re.compile(r'^(?P<indent>[ \t]*)def\s+(?P<name>\w+)\s*'
                    r'\((?P<params>[^()]*)\)\s*:\s*$')
RETURN_RE = re.compile(r'^[ \t]*return\s+(?P<expr>\S.*?)\s*$')
FOR_RANGE_RE = re.compile(r'^(?P<indent>[ \t]*)for\s+(?P<var>\w+)\s+in\s+'
                          r'range\s*\((?P<args>[^()]*)\)\s*:\s*$')
FOR_ITER_RE = re.compile(r'^(?P<indent>[ \t]*)for\s+(?P<var>\w+)\s+in\s*'
                         r'(?P<open>[\[(])(?P<items>[^\[\]()]*)[\])]\s*:\s*$')
ASSIGN_RE = re.compile(r'^(?P<indent>[ \t]*)(?P<name>[A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*=\s*'
                       r'(?P<value>[^=\s].*?)\s*$')
CHAINED_ASSIGN_RE = re.compile(r'^[A-Za-z_]\w*\s*=[^=]')
AUGMENTED_RE = re.compile(r'^[ \t]*(?P<name>[A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*'
                          r'(?:\+|-|\*|/|//|%|\*\*|>>|<<|&|\||\^)=')
CLASS_RE = re.compile(r'^(?P<indent>[ \t]*)class\s+(?P<name>\w+)\s*'
                      r'(?:\((?P<bases>[^()]*)\))?\s*:\s*$')
TYPE_ALIAS_RE = re.compile(r'^(?P<indent>[ \t]*)(?P<name>\w+)\s*=\s*'
                           r'(?:collections\.)?(?P<factory>namedtuple|NamedTuple'
                           r'|TypedDict|Enum|IntEnum|dataclass|type)\s*\(')
LITERAL_RE = re.compile(r'\[\s*\]|\{\s*\}|\(\s*\)|None|True|False'
                        r'|-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?|-?0[xXoObB][0-9a-fA-F]+')
ATOM_RE = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z_]\w*(?:\.\w+)*|-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?'
                     r'|\[\s*\]|\{\s*\}|None|True|False')
COMPREHENSION_RE = re.compile(r'\bfor\b')
BREAK_RE = re.compile(r'\b(?:break|continue|yield)\b')
CONTAINER_CALL_RE = re.compile(r'(?P<name>\b(?:dict|list|set|tuple|frozenset)\s*)$')

#: Characters that, outside brackets, mean an expression needs parentheses when
#: it is substituted into a larger one.
TOP_LEVEL_OPERATORS = set('+-*/%<>=!&|^,~')
TOP_LEVEL_KEYWORDS = frozenset({'if', 'else', 'for', 'and', 'or', 'not', 'in',
                                'is', 'lambda'})


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Text helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def code_segments(text: str) -> List[str]:
    """Split `text` into alternating code and string-literal fragments.

    The even indices hold code, the odd ones hold string literals, so a caller
    can rewrite identifiers without touching the inside of a string.
    """
    return STRING_RE.split(text)


def sub_outside_strings(pattern: re.Pattern,
                        repl: Callable[[re.Match], str],
                        text: str) -> Tuple[str, int]:
    """Apply `pattern` to the code parts of `text` only.

    Args:
        pattern: Compiled pattern to replace.
        repl: Replacement callable, as for :func:`re.sub`.
        text: Text to rewrite.

    Returns:
        The rewritten text and the number of replacements made.
    """
    parts = code_segments(text)
    count = 0
    for index in range(0, len(parts), 2):
        parts[index], made = pattern.subn(repl, parts[index])
        count += made
    return "".join(parts), count


def count_outside_strings(pattern: re.Pattern, text: str) -> int:
    """Number of matches of `pattern` in the code parts of `text`."""
    parts = code_segments(text)
    return sum(len(pattern.findall(parts[i])) for i in range(0, len(parts), 2))


def word_re(name: str) -> re.Pattern:
    """Pattern matching `name` as a whole word."""
    return re.compile(rf'\b{re.escape(name)}\b')


def indent_width(line: str) -> int:
    """Number of leading whitespace characters of `line`."""
    return len(line) - len(line.lstrip())


def is_blank(line: str) -> bool:
    """Whether `line` holds no code."""
    return not line.strip()


def block_end(lines: Sequence[str], start: int, header_indent: int) -> int:
    """Index just past the block that starts at `start`.

    The block covers every line indented deeper than `header_indent`, blank
    lines included.

    Args:
        lines: All lines of the program.
        start: First line of the block body.
        header_indent: Indentation of the header line.

    Returns:
        Index of the first line that no longer belongs to the block.
    """
    end = start
    for index in range(start, len(lines)):
        if is_blank(lines[index]):
            continue
        if indent_width(lines[index]) <= header_indent:
            return end
        end = index + 1
    return end


def dedent(line: str, amount: int) -> str:
    """Remove up to `amount` leading spaces from `line`."""
    if amount <= 0:
        return line
    stripped = 0
    while stripped < amount and line[:1] in (' ', '\t'):
        line = line[1:]
        stripped += 1
    return line


def split_top_level(text: str, separator: str = ',') -> List[str]:
    """Split `text` on separators that are not nested or quoted.

    Args:
        text: Text to split.
        separator: One-character separator.

    Returns:
        The stripped fragments; an empty list for text without content.
    """
    parts: List[str] = []
    depth = 0
    quote: Optional[str] = None
    current = ""
    index = 0
    while index < len(text):
        char = text[index]
        if quote is not None:
            current += char
            if char == '\\':
                if index + 1 < len(text):
                    current += text[index + 1]
                    index += 1
            elif char == quote:
                quote = None
        elif char in ('"', "'"):
            quote = char
            current += char
        elif char in '([{':
            depth += 1
            current += char
        elif char in ')]}':
            depth -= 1
            current += char
        elif char == separator and depth == 0:
            parts.append(current.strip())
            current = ""
        else:
            current += char
        index += 1
    if current.strip():
        parts.append(current.strip())
    return [part for part in parts if part]


def bracket_groups(text: str) -> List[Tuple[int, int, str]]:
    """Balanced bracket groups of `text`, leftmost-outermost first.

    Args:
        text: Text to scan (quotes are skipped).

    Returns:
        List of ``(start, end, opening_char)`` with `end` exclusive.
    """
    groups: List[Tuple[int, int, str]] = []
    stack: List[Tuple[int, str]] = []
    quote: Optional[str] = None
    index = 0
    while index < len(text):
        char = text[index]
        if quote is not None:
            if char == '\\':
                index += 2
                continue
            if char == quote:
                quote = None
        elif char in ('"', "'"):
            quote = char
        elif char in '([{':
            stack.append((index, char))
        elif char in ')]}':
            if stack:
                start, opening = stack.pop()
                groups.append((start, index + 1, opening))
        index += 1
    groups.sort(key=lambda group: (group[0], -group[1]))
    return groups


def needs_parens(expr: str) -> bool:
    """Whether `expr` must be parenthesized before being substituted."""
    depth = 0
    quote: Optional[str] = None
    word = ""
    for char in expr:
        if quote is not None:
            if char == quote:
                quote = None
            continue
        if char in ('"', "'"):
            quote = char
            continue
        if char in '([{':
            depth += 1
        elif char in ')]}':
            depth -= 1
        elif depth == 0:
            if char in TOP_LEVEL_OPERATORS:
                return True
            if char.isalnum() or char == '_':
                word += char
                continue
        word = ""
        if word in TOP_LEVEL_KEYWORDS:
            return True
    if depth == 0:
        for token in re.findall(r'\b\w+\b', expr):
            if token in TOP_LEVEL_KEYWORDS:
                return True
    return False


def is_atomic(expr: str) -> bool:
    """Whether `expr` is a single atom that never needs parentheses."""
    expr = expr.strip()
    if not expr:
        return False
    if STRING_RE.fullmatch(expr):
        return True
    return bool(ATOM_RE.fullmatch(expr))


def is_literal(expr: str) -> bool:
    """Whether `expr` is a literal, i.e. free to duplicate."""
    expr = expr.strip()
    if STRING_RE.fullmatch(expr):
        return True
    return bool(LITERAL_RE.fullmatch(expr))


def tidy(lines: Sequence[str]) -> str:
    """Join `lines` into a program, dropping blank lines at either end."""
    result = [line.rstrip() for line in lines]
    while result and is_blank(result[0]):
        result.pop(0)
    while result and is_blank(result[-1]):
        result.pop()
    if not result:
        return ""
    return "\n".join(result) + "\n"


def parenthesize(expr: str) -> str:
    """Wrap `expr` in parentheses when substituting it requires them."""
    return f"({expr})" if needs_parens(expr) else expr


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Responses
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@dataclass
class LLMResponse:
    """What the mock "model" answered for one prompt.

    Attributes:
        kind: The transformation that was requested.
        prompt: The prompt the mock was given.
        original: The program that was sent.
        source: The program with every found opportunity applied.
        edits: One human-readable description per applied rewrite.
        candidates: Programs with exactly one rewrite applied each, in the order
            they were found.  Used as a fallback when the cumulative rewrite
            breaks the property.
    """

    kind: str
    prompt: str
    original: str
    source: str
    edits: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    candidates: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def changed(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the model proposed anything at all."""
        return self.source != self.original

    @property
    def proposals(self) -> List[str]:
        """Every distinct program the model proposed, biggest rewrite first."""
        seen = {self.original}
        result = []
        for candidate in [self.source] + list(self.candidates):
            if candidate and candidate not in seen:
                seen.add(candidate)
                result.append(candidate)
        return result

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.edits)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (f"LLMResponse({self.kind}, edits={len(self.edits)}, "
                f"candidates={len(self.candidates)})")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# The mock model
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
class MockLLM:
    """Deterministic regex-based replacement for an LLM.

    Args:
        max_unroll: Largest iteration count :meth:`unroll_loops` expands.
        max_edits: Upper bound on the rewrites combined into the cumulative
            answer, so a pathological program cannot spin forever.
        max_candidates: Upper bound on the single-edit candidates reported.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        max_unroll: int = DEFAULT_MAX_UNROLL,
        max_edits: int = DEFAULT_MAX_EDITS,
        max_candidates: int = DEFAULT_MAX_CANDIDATES,
    ):
        self.max_unroll = max(1, max_unroll)
        self.max_edits = max(1, max_edits)
        self.max_candidates = max(1, max_candidates)
        self._call_count = 0
        self._prompts: List[str] = []

    @property
    def call_count(self) -> int:
        """Number of :meth:`transform` calls served so far."""
        return self._call_count

    @property
    def prompts(self) -> List[str]:
        """The prompts served so far, in order."""
        return list(self._prompts)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Prompting
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    @staticmethod
    def supports(kind: str) -> bool:
        """Whether `kind` is one of the five known transformations."""
        return kind in TRANSFORMATIONS

    def prompt_for(self, source: str, kind: str) -> str:
        """Build the prompt that would be sent to a real model.

        Args:
            source: Program to transform.
            kind: One of :data:`TRANSFORMATIONS`.

        Returns:
            The prompt text.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If `kind` is unknown.
        """
        if not self.supports(kind):
            raise ValueError(f"unknown transformation: {kind!r}")
        return (f"{SYSTEM_PROMPT}\n\n"
                f"Task: {kind}\n"
                f"{INSTRUCTIONS[kind]}\n\n"
                f"```python\n{source}```\n")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Main entry point
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    def transform(self, source: str, kind: str) -> LLMResponse:
        """Answer one transformation request.

        The cumulative answer is produced by applying the first opportunity,
        re-scanning the result and repeating; that way rewrites that only become
        possible after an earlier one (inlining a function whose body was just
        simplified) are found too.

        Args:
            source: Program to transform.
            kind: One of :data:`TRANSFORMATIONS`.

        Returns:
            The :class:`LLMResponse` describing what the mock came up with.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If `kind` is unknown.
        """
        prompt = self.prompt_for(source, kind)
        self._call_count += 1
        self._prompts.append(prompt)

        found = self.opportunities(source, kind)
        candidates = [text for text, _ in found[:self.max_candidates]]

        current = source
        edits: List[str] = []
        while len(edits) < self.max_edits:
            options = self.opportunities(current, kind)
            if not options:
                break
            text, description = options[0]
            if text == current or not text.strip():
                break
            current = text
            edits.append(description)

        return LLMResponse(kind=kind, prompt=prompt, original=source,
                           source=current, edits=edits, candidates=candidates)

    def opportunities(self, source: str, kind: str) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
        """Every single rewrite of `kind` that applies to `source`.

        Args:
            source: Program to inspect.
            kind: One of :data:`TRANSFORMATIONS`.

        Returns:
            List of ``(rewritten_program, description)``, in source order.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If `kind` is unknown.
        """
        handlers: Dict[str, Callable[[str], List[Tuple[str, str]]]] = {
            FUNCTION_INLINING: self.inline_functions,
            LOOP_UNROLLING: self.unroll_loops,
            VARIABLE_ELIMINATION: self.eliminate_variables,
            DATA_TYPE_ELIMINATION: self.eliminate_data_types,
            DATA_TYPE_SIMPLIFICATION: self.simplify_data_types,
        }
        if kind not in handlers:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown transformation: {kind!r}")
        return [item for item in handlers[kind](source) if item[0].strip()]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 1. function inlining
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    def inline_functions(self, source: str) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
        """Inline module-level functions whose body is a single return.

        Args:
            source: Program to inspect.

        Returns:
            One ``(program, description)`` entry per inlinable function.
        """
        lines = source.split('\n')
        results: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []

        for index, line in enumerate(lines):
            match = DEF_RE.match(line)
            if match is None or indent_width(line) != 0:
                # Methods need `self` bound to an instance, so only free
                # functions are inlined.
                continue
            name = match.group('name')
            params = self._parameters(match.group('params'))
            if params is None:
                continue
            end = block_end(lines, index + 1, 0)
            body = [text for text in lines[index + 1:end] if not is_blank(text)]
            if len(body) != 1:
                continue
            returned = RETURN_RE.match(body[0])
            if returned is None:
                continue
            expr = returned.group('expr')
            if count_outside_strings(word_re(name), expr):
                continue  # recursive: inlining would not terminate
            rest = lines[:index] + lines[end:]
            rewritten, calls = self._replace_calls('\n'.join(rest), name,
                                                   params, expr)
            if not calls:
                continue
            if count_outside_strings(word_re(name), rewritten):
                continue  # the name is still used (passed around as a value)
            results.append((tidy(rewritten.split('\n')),
                            f"inlined {name}() at {calls} call site(s)"))
        return results

    @staticmethod
    def _parameters(text: str) -> Optional[List[str]]:
        """Plain positional parameter names, or ``None`` when unsupported."""
        params = split_top_level(text)
        names = []
        for param in params:
            if not re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z_]\w*', param):
                return None  # defaults, *args, **kwargs, annotations
            names.append(param)
        return names

    def _replace_calls(self, text: str, name: str, params: Sequence[str],
                       expr: str) -> Tuple[str, int]:
        """Replace ``name(...)`` calls in `text` by the inlined expression.

        Args:
            text: Program without the function definition.
            name: Function name.
            params: Its positional parameters.
            expr: The returned expression.

        Returns:
            The rewritten text and the number of call sites replaced.
        """
        call = re.compile(rf'\b{re.escape(name)}\s*\((?P<args>[^()]*)\)')

        def substitute(match: re.Match) -> str:
            args = split_top_level(match.group('args'))
            if len(args) != len(params):
                return match.group(0)
            return parenthesize(self._bind(expr, params, args))

        # Count only the calls that were really rewritten.
        before = count_outside_strings(call, text)
        rewritten, _ = sub_outside_strings(call, substitute, text)
        after = count_outside_strings(call, rewritten)
        return rewritten, max(0, before - after)

    @staticmethod
    def _bind(expr: str, params: Sequence[str],
              args: Sequence[str]) -> str:
        """Substitute `args` for `params` in `expr` in a single pass."""
        if not params:
            return expr
        mapping = {
            param: (arg if is_atomic(arg) else f"({arg})")
            for param, arg in zip(params, args)
        }
        pattern = re.compile(
            r'\b(' + '|'.join(re.escape(p) for p in params) + r')\b')
        bound, _ = sub_outside_strings(pattern,
                                       lambda m: mapping[m.group(1)], expr)
        return bound

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 2. loop unrolling
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    def unroll_loops(self, source: str) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
        """Replace bounded ``for`` loops by their iterations.

        Args:
            source: Program to inspect.

        Returns:
            One ``(program, description)`` entry per unrollable loop.
        """
        lines = source.split('\n')
        results: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []

        for index, line in enumerate(lines):
            header = FOR_RANGE_RE.match(line) or FOR_ITER_RE.match(line)
            if header is None:
                continue
            values = self._loop_values(header)
            if values is None:
                continue
            loop_indent = indent_width(line)
            end = block_end(lines, index + 1, loop_indent)
            body = lines[index + 1:end]
            if not [text for text in body if not is_blank(text)]:
                continue
            if any(count_outside_strings(BREAK_RE, text) for text in body):
                continue  # break/continue/yield do not survive unrolling
            var = header.group('var')
            if self._used_after(lines, end, var):
                continue  # Python leaks the loop variable

            body_indent = min(indent_width(text) for text in body
                              if not is_blank(text))
            shift = body_indent - loop_indent
            if not values:
                replacement = [' ' * loop_indent + 'pass']
                description = f"dropped zero-iteration loop over {var}"
            else:
                replacement = []
                for value in values:
                    for text in body:
                        if is_blank(text):
                            continue
                        bound, _ = sub_outside_strings(
                            word_re(var), lambda _m, v=value: v,
                            dedent(text, shift))
                        replacement.append(bound)
                description = (f"unrolled loop over {var} into "
                               f"{len(values)} iteration(s)")
            rewritten = lines[:index] + replacement + lines[end:]
            results.append((tidy(rewritten), description))
        return results

    def _loop_values(self, header: re.Match) -> Optional[List[str]]:
        """Literal values the loop iterates over, or ``None`` when unknown."""
        groups = header.groupdict()
        if 'args' in groups:
            bounds = []
            for arg in split_top_level(groups['args']):
                if not re.fullmatch(r'-?\d+', arg):
                    return None
                bounds.append(int(arg))
            if not 1 <= len(bounds) <= 3:
                return None
            if len(bounds) == 3 and bounds[2] == 0:
                return None
            values = list(range(*bounds))
            if len(values) > self.max_unroll:
                return None
            return [str(value) for value in values]

        items = split_top_level(groups.get('items', ''))
        if not items or len(items) > self.max_unroll:
            return None
        if not all(is_literal(item) or STRING_RE.fullmatch(item)
                   for item in items):
            return None
        return items

    @staticmethod
    def _used_after(lines: Sequence[str], start: int, name: str) -> bool:
        """Whether `name` still occurs from line `start` onwards."""
        pattern = word_re(name)
        return any(count_outside_strings(pattern, text)
                   for text in lines[start:])

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 3. variable elimination
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    def eliminate_variables(self, source: str) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
        """Propagate single-assignment variables into their uses.

        A variable qualifies when it is assigned exactly once, every use is
        inside the assignment's own block and after it, and either the value is
        a literal (free to duplicate) or there is exactly one use.

        Args:
            source: Program to inspect.

        Returns:
            One ``(program, description)`` entry per eliminable variable.
        """
        lines = source.split('\n')
        results: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []

        for index, line in enumerate(lines):
            match = ASSIGN_RE.match(line)
            if match is None:
                continue
            name = match.group('name')
            value = match.group('value')
            if name in RESERVED or CHAINED_ASSIGN_RE.match(value):
                continue
            if count_outside_strings(word_re(name), value):
                continue  # self-referential, e.g. `x = x + 1`
            if not self._assigned_once(lines, index, name):
                continue

            scope = self._scope_end(lines, index)
            uses = [other for other in range(index + 1, scope)
                    if count_outside_strings(word_re(name), lines[other])]
            outside = [other for other in range(len(lines))
                       if other != index
                       and not (index < other < scope)
                       and count_outside_strings(word_re(name), lines[other])]
            if outside or not uses:
                continue
            total = sum(count_outside_strings(word_re(name), lines[other])
                        for other in uses)
            if total > 1 and not is_literal(value):
                continue  # duplicating a computation may change behaviour

            replacement = parenthesize(value)
            rewritten = list(lines)
            for other in uses:
                rewritten[other], _ = sub_outside_strings(
                    word_re(name), lambda _m: replacement, rewritten[other])
            del rewritten[index]
            results.append((tidy(rewritten),
                            f"eliminated variable {name} ({total} use(s))"))
        return results

    @staticmethod
    def _assigned_once(lines: Sequence[str], index: int, name: str) -> bool:
        """Whether `name` is bound exactly once, on line `index`."""
        pattern = word_re(name)
        binders = (
            re.compile(rf'\bfor\s+{re.escape(name)}\b'),
            re.compile(rf'\bdef\s+{re.escape(name)}\b'),
            re.compile(rf'\bclass\s+{re.escape(name)}\b'),
            re.compile(rf'\b(?:global|nonlocal|del)\s+[\w\s,]*'
                       rf'\b{re.escape(name)}\b'),
            re.compile(rf'\bas\s+{re.escape(name)}\b'),
            re.compile(rf'\bimport\s+[\w\s,.]*\b{re.escape(name)}\b'),
            re.compile(rf'\bwith\s+.*\b{re.escape(name)}\b\s*:'),
        )
        for other, line in enumerate(lines):
            if other == index:
                continue
            if not count_outside_strings(pattern, line):
                continue
            assigned = ASSIGN_RE.match(line)
            if assigned is not None and assigned.group('name') == name:
                return False
            augmented = AUGMENTED_RE.match(line)
            if augmented is not None and augmented.group('name') == name:
                return False
            if any(count_outside_strings(binder, line) for binder in binders):
                return False
            # A parameter with this name shadows the variable.
            definition = DEF_RE.match(line)
            if definition is not None and name in split_top_level(
                    definition.group('params')):
                return False
        return True

    @staticmethod
    def _scope_end(lines: Sequence[str], index: int) -> int:
        """Index just past the block the line at `index` belongs to."""
        indent = indent_width(lines[index])
        if indent == 0:
            return len(lines)
        for other in range(index + 1, len(lines)):
            if is_blank(lines[other]):
                continue
            if indent_width(lines[other]) < indent:
                return other
        return len(lines)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 4. data type elimination
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    def eliminate_data_types(self, source: str) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
        """Delete class and type definitions nothing references.

        Args:
            source: Program to inspect.

        Returns:
            One ``(program, description)`` entry per removable definition.
        """
        lines = source.split('\n')
        results: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []

        for index, line in enumerate(lines):
            match = CLASS_RE.match(line)
            if match is not None:
                name = match.group('name')
                end = block_end(lines, index + 1, indent_width(line))
                if self._referenced_outside(lines, index, end, name):
                    continue
                rewritten = lines[:index] + lines[end:]
                results.append((tidy(rewritten),
                                f"removed unused class {name}"))
                continue

            alias = TYPE_ALIAS_RE.match(line)
            if alias is not None:
                name = alias.group('name')
                if self._referenced_outside(lines, index, index + 1, name):
                    continue
                rewritten = lines[:index] + lines[index + 1:]
                results.append((tidy(rewritten),
                                f"removed unused type alias {name}"))
        return results

    @staticmethod
    def _referenced_outside(lines: Sequence[str], start: int, end: int,
                            name: str) -> bool:
        """Whether `name` occurs outside the ``[start, end)`` line range."""
        pattern = word_re(name)
        return any(count_outside_strings(pattern, line)
                   for index, line in enumerate(lines)
                   if not start <= index < end)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 5. data type simplification
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    def simplify_data_types(self, source: str) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
        """Collapse composite data structures into simpler shapes.

        The rules are: a non-empty dict/set literal becomes ``{}``, a
        comprehension becomes the empty container, a literal with several
        elements keeps only its first one, and a ``dict(...)``/``list(...)``
        style constructor call loses its arguments.

        Args:
            source: Program to inspect.

        Returns:
            One ``(program, description)`` entry per simplification.
        """
        lines = source.split('\n')
        results: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []

        for index, line in enumerate(lines):
            for start, end, opening in bracket_groups(line):
                inner = line[start + 1:end - 1]
                simplified = self._simplify_group(line, start, opening, inner)
                if simplified is None:
                    continue
                replacement, description = simplified
                if replacement == line[start:end]:
                    continue
                rewritten = list(lines)
                rewritten[index] = line[:start] + replacement + line[end:]
                results.append((tidy(rewritten), f"{description} on line "
                                                 f"{index + 1}"))
        return results

    def _simplify_group(self, line: str, start: int, opening: str,
                        inner: str) -> Optional[Tuple[str, str]]:
        """Simplification for one bracket group, or ``None`` when there is none.

        Args:
            line: The line holding the group.
            start: Index of the opening bracket.
            opening: The opening bracket character.
            inner: Text between the brackets.

        Returns:
            ``(replacement_text, description)`` or ``None``.
        """
        prefix = line[:start]
        stripped = inner.strip()

        if opening == '(':
            container = CONTAINER_CALL_RE.search(prefix)
            if container is not None and stripped:
                return "()", (f"emptied "
                              f"{container.group('name').strip()}() call")
            return None

        empty = '[]' if opening == '[' else '{}'
        if not stripped:
            return None
        if count_outside_strings(COMPREHENSION_RE, inner):
            return empty, "collapsed comprehension"
        if opening == '{':
            return empty, "collapsed dict/set literal"
        elements = split_top_level(inner)
        if len(elements) > 1:
            return f"[{elements[0]}]", (f"kept 1 of {len(elements)} list "
                                        f"elements")
        return None

"""LLM-driven reducers, the reduction half of LPR.

Each reducer here owns one of the five transformation types of
:mod:`reduction.lpr.mock_llm` and drives the same three-step loop LPR uses with
a real model:

1. render the current SparTree back to source and send it to the model;
2. take the program the model answers with;
3. keep it only when it is smaller *and* the property still holds - otherwise
   throw it away and leave the tree untouched.

Step 3 is what makes an unreliable model usable: the LLM is free to propose a
program that no longer compiles or no longer triggers the bug, and the property
tester filters those out.  Because a rewritten program has no relation to the
old tree, an accepted answer is re-parsed into a fresh SparTree, which the
syntax-guided reducers (Perses, Vulcan) then keep working on.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from abc import abstractmethod
from typing import List, Optional

from reduction.grammar import Grammar
from reduction.lpr.mock_llm import (DATA_TYPE_ELIMINATION,
                                    DATA_TYPE_SIMPLIFICATION,
                                    FUNCTION_INLINING, LOOP_UNROLLING,
                                    TRANSFORMATIONS, VARIABLE_ELIMINATION,
                                    LLMResponse, MockLLM)
from reduction.parser import Parser
from reduction.property_test import PropertyTester
from reduction.reducer import AbstractReducer
from reduction.tree import SparTreeNode


class LLMReducer(AbstractReducer):
    """Base class for the reducers that ask the model for a rewrite.

    Args:
        grammar: Grammar used to re-parse an accepted answer.  Defaults to the
            simplified Python grammar.
        llm: The model to query.  Defaults to a fresh :class:`MockLLM`;
            sharing one instance between reducers makes the call counts add up
            over the whole pipeline.
        try_single_edits: When the model's full rewrite is rejected, retry with
            the individual edits it proposed.  This is what keeps one bad
            rewrite from throwing away the good ones.
        max_tests: Property test budget per :meth:`reduce` call.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        grammar: Grammar | None = None,
        llm: MockLLM | None = None,
        try_single_edits: bool = True,
        max_tests: int | None = None,
    ):
        self.grammar = grammar or Grammar.python_simplified()
        self.llm = llm or MockLLM()
        self.try_single_edits = try_single_edits
        self.max_tests = max_tests
        self.parser = Parser(self.grammar)
        self._tests_used = 0
        self._response: Optional[LLMResponse] = None
        self._applied: List[str] = []

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Identity
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def transformation(self) -> str:
        """The :data:`~reduction.lpr.mock_llm.TRANSFORMATIONS` entry to request."""
        ...

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """The name of this reduction algorithm."""
        return f"LPR-{self.transformation}"

    @property
    def tests_used(self) -> int:
        """Property tests issued during the last :meth:`reduce` call."""
        return self._tests_used

    @property
    def last_response(self) -> Optional[LLMResponse]:
        """The model's answer to the last :meth:`reduce` call."""
        return self._response

    @property
    def applied_edits(self) -> List[str]:
        """Descriptions of the rewrites accepted by the last :meth:`reduce`."""
        return list(self._applied)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Reduction
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    def reduce(self, tree: SparTreeNode, tester: PropertyTester) -> SparTreeNode:
        """Ask the model for a rewrite and keep it if the property survives.

        Args:
            tree: SparTree to reduce.
            tester: Property tester validating the model's answer.

        Returns:
            A freshly parsed tree for the accepted rewrite, or `tree` unchanged
            when the model had nothing usable to offer.
        """
        self._tests_used = 0
        self._response = None
        self._applied = []

        source = tree.to_source()
        if not source.strip():
            return tree

        response = self.llm.transform(source, self.transformation)
        self._response = response
        if not response.changed:
            return tree

        baseline = tree.token_count()
        for proposal in response.proposals:
            if self.max_tests is not None and self._tests_used >= self.max_tests:
                break
            candidate = self.parser.parse(proposal)
            # The tree is what the rest of the pipeline works on, so the tree's
            # own rendering - not the model's text - is what gets validated.
            text = candidate.to_source()
            if not text.strip() or candidate.token_count() >= baseline:
                continue
            self._tests_used += 1
            if tester.test(text):
                self._applied = response.describe(proposal)
                return candidate
            if not self.try_single_edits:
                break
        return tree


class FunctionInliningReducer(LLMReducer):
    """Replace calls of a one-line function by its body."""

    @property
    def transformation(self) -> str:
        """The transformation this reducer requests."""
        return FUNCTION_INLINING


class LoopUnrollingReducer(LLMReducer):
    """Replace a loop with a known small trip count by its iterations."""

    @property
    def transformation(self) -> str:
        """The transformation this reducer requests."""
        return LOOP_UNROLLING


class VariableEliminationReducer(LLMReducer):
    """Propagate a variable's value into its uses and drop the assignment."""

    @property
    def transformation(self) -> str:
        """The transformation this reducer requests."""
        return VARIABLE_ELIMINATION


class DataTypeEliminationReducer(LLMReducer):
    """Delete class and type definitions nothing references."""

    @property
    def transformation(self) -> str:
        """The transformation this reducer requests."""
        return DATA_TYPE_ELIMINATION


class DataTypeSimplificationReducer(LLMReducer):
    """Collapse composite data structures into simpler shapes."""

    @property
    def transformation(self) -> str:
        """The transformation this reducer requests."""
        return DATA_TYPE_SIMPLIFICATION


#: The reducer class implementing each transformation type.
REDUCER_CLASSES = {
    FUNCTION_INLINING: FunctionInliningReducer,
    LOOP_UNROLLING: LoopUnrollingReducer,
    VARIABLE_ELIMINATION: VariableEliminationReducer,
    DATA_TYPE_ELIMINATION: DataTypeEliminationReducer,
    DATA_TYPE_SIMPLIFICATION: DataTypeSimplificationReducer,
}


def llm_reducers(grammar: Grammar | None = None,
                 llm: MockLLM | None = None,
                 kinds: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> List[LLMReducer]:
    """One reducer per transformation type, sharing a single model.

    Args:
        grammar: Grammar handed to every reducer.
        llm: Model to share; a fresh :class:`MockLLM` when omitted, so that
            :attr:`MockLLM.call_count` totals the whole pipeline.
        kinds: Transformations to include; all five by default.

    Returns:
        The reducers, in the order LPR applies them.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If `kinds` names an unknown transformation.
    """
    model = llm or MockLLM()
    selected = list(kinds) if kinds is not None else list(TRANSFORMATIONS)
    unknown = [kind for kind in selected if kind not in REDUCER_CLASSES]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown transformations: {unknown}")
    return [REDUCER_CLASSES[kind](grammar, model) for kind in selected]

"""LPR: large language model-aided program reduction.

Syntax-guided reducers can only cut a program apart along its parse tree.  Some
of the reductions a human would do are *rewrites* instead: inlining a helper,
unrolling a loop, propagating a constant.  LPR gets those from a language model
and validates every answer with the property tester, which is what makes an
unreliable model safe to use inside a reducer.

The package has two halves:

* :mod:`reduction.lpr.mock_llm` - a deterministic, regex-driven stand-in for the
  model, so the benchmark needs neither a network nor a random seed;
* :mod:`reduction.lpr.llm_reducer` - the five
  :class:`~reduction.lpr.llm_reducer.LLMReducer` subclasses that ask for one
  transformation type each and keep the answer only when the program got
  smaller and the property held.

:func:`~reduction.lpr.llm_reducer.llm_reducers` returns all five, ready to be
inserted between the Perses and Vulcan passes of a
:class:`~reduction.driver.ReductionDriver`.

"""LPR: large language model-aided program reduction.

Syntax-guided reducers can only cut a program apart along its parse tree.  Some
of the reductions a human would do are *rewrites* instead: inlining a helper,
unrolling a loop, propagating a constant.  LPR gets those from a language model
and validates every answer with the property tester, which is what makes an
unreliable model safe to use inside a reducer.

The package has two halves:

* :mod:`reduction.lpr.mock_llm` - a deterministic, regex-driven stand-in for the
  model, so the benchmark needs neither a network nor a random seed;
* :mod:`reduction.lpr.llm_reducer` - the five
  :class:`~reduction.lpr.llm_reducer.LLMReducer` subclasses that ask for one
  transformation type each and keep the answer only when the program got
  smaller and the property held.

:func:`~reduction.lpr.llm_reducer.llm_reducers` returns all five, ready to be
inserted between the Perses and Vulcan passes of a
:class:`~reduction.driver.ReductionDriver`.
"""

#!/bin/bash
# Experiment runner for the Perses-family program reduction benchmark.
#
# Every experiment is a self-contained Python 3 (standard library only) block
# that prints its metrics as `KEY=value` lines.  Reduced programs are echoed
# with a leading "  | " so that they never look like metric lines.
#
# Sections:
#   1. Perses  - DD baseline + syntax-guided reduction (bug1/bug2/bug3)
#   2. Vulcan  - Perses + the three 1-minimality reducers (bug1/bug2/bug3)
#   3. PPR     - pairwise reduction of the seed/variant pair (ppr_bug1)

set -u

cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
PYTHON=${PYTHON:-python3}

section() {
    echo
    echo "=== $1 ==="
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# 1. Perses: syntax-guided reduction vs the delta-debugging baseline
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
section "Perses: DD baseline and syntax-guided reduction"
"$PYTHON" - <<'PY'
from reduction import (Config, DeltaDebugging, Grammar, PropertyTester,
                       ReductionDriver, Tokenizer)
from reduction.perses_reducer import PersesReducer
from reduction.pnf import normalize, validate_pnf

BUGS = ("bug1", "bug2", "bug3")


def emit(key, value):
    print(f"{key}={value}")


def show(source, limit=40):
    for line in source.rstrip("\n").split("\n")[:limit]:
        print(f"  | {line}")


def ratio(original, reduced):
    if original == 0:
        return 0.0
    return round(1.0 - reduced / original, 4)


def read(path):
    with open(path) as handle:
        return handle.read()


# The grammar the reducer reasons about is normalized into Prioritized Normal
# Form first; PNF is what makes the quantifier/compatibility logic sound.
grammar = normalize(Grammar.python_simplified())
problems = validate_pnf(grammar)
emit("PNF_RULES", len(grammar.rules))
emit("PNF_VALID", int(not problems))
for problem in problems:
    print(f"  ! {problem}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- DD baseline
source = read("test_subjects/bug1/program.py")
tokens = [t for t in Tokenizer().tokenize(source) if t.type != "NEWLINE"]
tester = PropertyTester("test_subjects/bug1/test.sh")
dd = DeltaDebugging(tester)
dd_reduced = dd.reduce(tokens)
emit("DD_BUG1_ORIGINAL", len(tokens))
emit("DD_BUG1_TOKENS", len(dd_reduced))
emit("DD_BUG1_TESTS", tester.test_count)
emit("DD_BUG1_RATIO", ratio(len(tokens), len(dd_reduced)))
show(dd._tokens_to_source(dd_reduced))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- Perses
for bug in BUGS:
    source = read(f"test_subjects/{bug}/program.py")
    tester = PropertyTester(f"test_subjects/{bug}/test.sh")
    driver = ReductionDriver(grammar, tester, [PersesReducer(grammar)], Config())
    result = driver.reduce(source)
    key = bug.upper()
    emit(f"PERSES_{key}_ORIGINAL", result.original_tokens)
    emit(f"PERSES_{key}_TOKENS", result.reduced_tokens)
    emit(f"PERSES_{key}_TESTS", result.num_tests)
    emit(f"PERSES_{key}_RATIO", round(result.reduction_ratio, 4))
    show(result.reduced_source)
PY

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# 2. Vulcan: Perses followed by the three 1-minimality reducers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
section "Vulcan: pushing the limit of 1-minimality"
"$PYTHON" - <<'PY'
from reduction import Config, Grammar, PropertyTester, ReductionDriver
from reduction.perses_reducer import PersesReducer
from reduction.pnf import normalize
from reduction.vulcan import (IdentifierReplacementReducer,
                              LocalExhaustiveReducer,
                              SubtreeReplacementReducer)

BUGS = ("bug1", "bug2", "bug3")


def emit(key, value):
    print(f"{key}={value}")


def show(source, limit=40):
    for line in source.rstrip("\n").split("\n")[:limit]:
        print(f"  | {line}")


def read(path):
    with open(path) as handle:
        return handle.read()


grammar = normalize(Grammar.python_simplified())

for bug in BUGS:
    source = read(f"test_subjects/{bug}/program.py")
    tester = PropertyTester(f"test_subjects/{bug}/test.sh")
    # Perses first (it does the heavy structural work), then the Vulcan
    # strategies that keep going past Perses' 1-minimality.
    reducers = [
        PersesReducer(grammar),
        IdentifierReplacementReducer(),
        SubtreeReplacementReducer(grammar),
        LocalExhaustiveReducer(grammar, window_size=3, budget=200),
    ]
    result = ReductionDriver(grammar, tester, reducers, Config()).reduce(source)
    key = bug.upper()
    emit(f"VULCAN_{key}_ORIGINAL", result.original_tokens)
    emit(f"VULCAN_{key}_TOKENS", result.reduced_tokens)
    emit(f"VULCAN_{key}_TESTS", result.num_tests)
    emit(f"VULCAN_{key}_RATIO", round(result.reduction_ratio, 4))
    show(result.reduced_source)
PY

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# 3. PPR: pairwise reduction of a seed/variant pair
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
section "PPR: pairwise program reduction"
"$PYTHON" - <<'PY'
from ppr import PPRDriver, line_diff, token_diff
from reduction import Config, Grammar, PropertyTester
from reduction.pnf import normalize

SUBJECT = "test_subjects/ppr_bug1"


def emit(key, value):
    print(f"{key}={value}")


def show(source, limit=40):
    for line in source.rstrip("\n").split("\n")[:limit]:
        print(f"  | {line}")


def read(path):
    with open(path) as handle:
        return handle.read()


grammar = normalize(Grammar.python_simplified())
seed = read(f"{SUBJECT}/seed.py")
variant = read(f"{SUBJECT}/variant.py")
seed_tester = PropertyTester(f"{SUBJECT}/test_seed.sh")
variant_tester = PropertyTester(f"{SUBJECT}/test_variant.sh")

driver = PPRDriver(grammar, seed_tester, variant_tester, Config())
result = driver.reduce(seed, variant)

emit("PPR_SEED_ORIGINAL", result.seed_original_tokens)
emit("PPR_SEED_REDUCED", result.seed_reduced_tokens)
emit("PPR_VARIANT_ORIGINAL", result.variant_original_tokens)
emit("PPR_VARIANT_REDUCED", result.variant_reduced_tokens)
emit("PPR_DIFF_ORIGINAL", result.diff_original_tokens)
emit("PPR_DIFF_REDUCED", result.diff_reduced_tokens)
emit("PPR_NUM_TESTS", result.num_tests)
emit("PPR_SEED_RATIO", round(result.seed_ratio, 4))
emit("PPR_VARIANT_RATIO", round(result.variant_ratio, 4))
emit("PPR_DIFF_RATIO", round(result.diff_ratio, 4))
emit("PPR_ITERATIONS", result.iterations)
emit("PPR_HUNKS", len(line_diff(result.seed_source, result.variant_source)))

print("  --- reduced seed ---")
show(result.seed_source)
print("  --- reduced variant ---")
show(result.variant_source)
print("  --- surviving difference ---")
final = token_diff(result.seed_source, result.variant_source)
print(f"  | seed only:    {' '.join(final.only_left)}")
print(f"  | variant only: {' '.join(final.only_right)}")
PY

def always():
    """A tester every non-empty candidate satisfies."""
    return FakeTester(lambda source: bool(source.strip()))


def never():
    """A tester nothing satisfies."""
    return FakeTester(lambda source: False)


def requires(*needles):
    """A tester satisfied only while every needle is present."""
    return FakeTester(lambda source: all(n in source for n in needles))

        self.assertEqual(split_top_level("'x, y', z"), ["'x, y'", "z"])
        self.assertEqual(split_top_level("   "), [])

        groups = bracket_groups("f(a[1], {2: 3})")

class VariableEliminationTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.llm = MockLLM()

    def test_propagates_a_single_use_variable(self):

        response = self.llm.transform(source, VARIABLE_ELIMINATION)
        self.assertIn("return sum(v) / 2", response.source)
        self.assertNotIn("t =", response.source)

        source = "n = 2\nprint(n)\nprint(n)\n"

        self.assertEqual(response.source, "print(2)\nprint(2)\n")

    def test_keeps_a_recomputed_value_used_twice(self):
        source = "n = sum(v)\nprint(n)\nprint(n)\n"
        self.assertFalse(self.llm.transform(source,
                                           VARIABLE_ELIMINATION).changed)

    def test_keeps_reassigned_and_augmented_variables(self):
        reassigned = "n = 1\nn = 2\nprint(n)\n"
        self.assertFalse(self.llm.transform(reassigned,
                                           VARIABLE_ELIMINATION).changed)
        augmented = "n = 1\nn += 1\nprint(n)\n"
        self.assertFalse(self.llm.transform(augmented,
                                           VARIABLE_ELIMINATION).changed)

    def test_keeps_unused_and_self_referential_assignments(self):
        unused = "n = 1\nprint(2)\n"
        self.assertFalse(self.llm.transform(unused,
                                           VARIABLE_ELIMINATION).changed)
        loop = "n = n + 1\nprint(n)\n"
        self.assertFalse(self.llm.transform(loop,
                                           VARIABLE_ELIMINATION).changed)

    def test_does_not_escape_its_block(self):
        source = "def f():\n    t = 1\nprint(t)\n"

                                           VARIABLE_ELIMINATION).changed)

        self.llm = MockLLM()

        self.assertEqual(response.source, "print(1)\n")

        self.assertFalse(self.llm.transform(source,
                                           DATA_TYPE_ELIMINATION).changed)

    def test_removes_an_unused_type_alias(self):

class LLMReducerTest(unittest.TestCase):
    SOURCE = "def h(x):\n    return x * 2\ny = h(5)\nprint(y)\n"

    def setUp(self):
        self.grammar = normalize(Grammar.python_simplified())
        self.parser = Parser(self.grammar)

    def parse(self, source):
        return self.parser.parse(source)

    def test_reducers_are_abstract_reducers_with_names(self):
        reducers = llm_reducers(self.grammar)
        self.assertEqual(len(reducers), len(TRANSFORMATIONS))
        for reducer in reducers:
            self.assertIsInstance(reducer, AbstractReducer)
            self.assertIsInstance(reducer, LLMReducer)
            self.assertTrue(reducer.name.startswith("LPR-"))
        self.assertEqual([r.transformation for r in reducers],
                         list(TRANSFORMATIONS))

    def test_shared_model_totals_the_calls(self):
        llm = MockLLM()
        tree = self.parse(self.SOURCE)
        for reducer in llm_reducers(self.grammar, llm):
            reducer.reduce(tree, never())
        self.assertEqual(llm.call_count, len(TRANSFORMATIONS))

    def test_unknown_kind_is_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            llm_reducers(self.grammar, kinds=["telepathy"])

    def test_accepted_rewrite_returns_a_smaller_tree(self):
        tree = self.parse(self.SOURCE)
        reducer = FunctionInliningReducer(self.grammar)
        reduced = reducer.reduce(tree, always())
        self.assertLess(reduced.token_count(), tree.token_count())
        self.assertNotIn("def h", reduced.to_source())
        self.assertEqual(reducer.tests_used, 1)
        self.assertTrue(reducer.applied_edits)

    def test_rejected_rewrite_keeps_the_original_tree(self):
        tree = self.parse(self.SOURCE)
        reducer = FunctionInliningReducer(self.grammar)
        reduced = reducer.reduce(tree, never())
        self.assertIs(reduced, tree)
        self.assertIn("def h", reduced.to_source())
        self.assertEqual(reducer.applied_edits, [])

    def test_falls_back_to_a_single_edit(self):
        # Only the dict may be collapsed; the list must keep its elements.
        source = "a = {'k': 1}\nb = [1, 2, 3]\nprint(a, b)\n"
        tree = self.parse(source)
        reducer = DataTypeSimplificationReducer(self.grammar)
        reduced = reducer.reduce(tree, requires("[ 1 , 2 , 3 ]"))
        text = reduced.to_source()
        self.assertIn("{ }", text)
        self.assertIn("[ 1 , 2 , 3 ]", text)
        self.assertGreater(reducer.tests_used, 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(reducer.applied_edits), 1)

    def test_single_edit_fallback_can_be_switched_off(self):
        source = "a = {'k': 1}\nb = [1, 2, 3]\nprint(a, b)\n"
        tree = self.parse(source)
        reducer = DataTypeSimplificationReducer(self.grammar,
                                               try_single_edits=False)
        reduced = reducer.reduce(tree, requires("[ 1 , 2 , 3 ]"))
        self.assertIs(reduced, tree)
        self.assertEqual(reducer.tests_used, 1)

    def test_no_opportunity_costs_no_test(self):
        tree = self.parse("print(1)\n")
        reducer = LoopUnrollingReducer(self.grammar)
        reduced = reducer.reduce(tree, always())
        self.assertIs(reduced, tree)
        self.assertEqual(reducer.tests_used, 0)
        self.assertFalse(reducer.last_response.changed)

    def test_budget_bounds_the_tests(self):
        source = "a = {'k': 1}\nb = [1, 2, 3]\nprint(a, b)\n"
        tree = self.parse(source)
        reducer = DataTypeSimplificationReducer(self.grammar, max_tests=1)
        reducer.reduce(tree, never())
        self.assertEqual(reducer.tests_used, 1)

    def test_every_concrete_reducer_reports_its_transformation(self):
        pairs = [
            (FunctionInliningReducer, FUNCTION_INLINING),
            (LoopUnrollingReducer, LOOP_UNROLLING),
            (VariableEliminationReducer, VARIABLE_ELIMINATION),
            (DataTypeEliminationReducer, DATA_TYPE_ELIMINATION),
            (DataTypeSimplificationReducer, DATA_TYPE_SIMPLIFICATION),
        ]
        for cls, kind in pairs:
            self.assertEqual(cls(self.grammar).transformation, kind)

    def test_empty_tree_is_left_alone(self):
        tree = self.parse("")
        reducer = FunctionInliningReducer(self.grammar)
        self.assertIs(reducer.reduce(tree, always()), tree)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

class LoopUnrollingTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.llm = MockLLM()

    def test_unrolls_a_small_range_loop(self):
        source = "t = 0\nfor i in range(3):\n    t += i\nprint(t)\n"
        response = self.llm.transform(source, LOOP_UNROLLING)
        self.assertIn("t += 0\nt += 1\nt += 2", response.source)
        self.assertNotIn("for", response.source)

    def test_unrolls_a_literal_list_loop(self):
        source = "for v in [1, 2]:\n    print(v)\n"
        response = self.llm.transform(source, LOOP_UNROLLING)
        self.assertIn("print(1)", response.source)
        self.assertIn("print(2)", response.source)

    def test_range_bounds_are_honoured(self):
        source = "for i in range(1, 3):\n    print(i)\n"
        response = self.llm.transform(source, LOOP_UNROLLING)
        self.assertIn("print(1)", response.source)
        self.assertIn("print(2)", response.source)
        self.assertNotIn("print(0)", response.source)

    def test_empty_range_becomes_pass(self):
        source = "for i in range(0):\n    print(i)\n"
        response = self.llm.transform(source, LOOP_UNROLLING)
        self.assertEqual(response.source, "pass\n")

    def test_refuses_unbounded_and_control_flow_loops(self):
        dynamic = "for v in values:\n    print(v)\n"
        self.assertFalse(self.llm.transform(dynamic, LOOP_UNROLLING).changed)
        big = "for i in range(100):\n    print(i)\n"
        self.assertFalse(self.llm.transform(big, LOOP_UNROLLING).changed)

        source = "for i in range(2):\n    print(i)\nprint(i)\n"
        self.assertFalse(self.llm.transform(source, LOOP_UNROLLING).changed)

    def test_nested_body_keeps_its_shape(self):
        source = "for i in range(2):\n    if i:\n        print(i)\n"
        response = self.llm.transform(source, LOOP_UNROLLING)
        self.assertIn("if 0:\n    print(0)", response.source)

class LLMReducerTest(unittest.TestCase):
    SOURCE = "def h(x):\n    return x * 2\ny = h(5)\nprint(y)\n"

    def setUp(self):
        self.grammar = normalize(Grammar.python_simplified())
        self.parser = Parser(self.grammar)

    def parse(self, source):
        return self.parser.parse(source)

    def test_reducers_are_abstract_reducers_with_names(self):
        reducers = llm_reducers(self.grammar)
        self.assertEqual(len(reducers), len(TRANSFORMATIONS))
        for reducer in reducers:
            self.assertIsInstance(reducer, AbstractReducer)
            self.assertIsInstance(reducer, LLMReducer)
            self.assertTrue(reducer.name.startswith("LPR-"))
        self.assertEqual([r.transformation for r in reducers],
                         list(TRANSFORMATIONS))

    def test_shared_model_totals_the_calls(self):
        llm = MockLLM()
        tree = self.parse(self.SOURCE)
        for reducer in llm_reducers(self.grammar, llm):
            reducer.reduce(tree, never())
        self.assertEqual(llm.call_count, len(TRANSFORMATIONS))

    def test_unknown_kind_is_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            llm_reducers(self.grammar, kinds=["telepathy"])

    def test_accepted_rewrite_returns_a_smaller_tree(self):
        tree = self.parse(self.SOURCE)
        reducer = FunctionInliningReducer(self.grammar)
        reduced = reducer.reduce(tree, always())
        self.assertLess(reduced.token_count(), tree.token_count())
        self.assertNotIn("def h", reduced.to_source())
        self.assertEqual(reducer.tests_used, 1)
        self.assertTrue(reducer.applied_edits)

    def test_rejected_rewrite_keeps_the_original_tree(self):
        tree = self.parse(self.SOURCE)
        reducer = FunctionInliningReducer(self.grammar)
        reduced = reducer.reduce(tree, never())
        self.assertIs(reduced, tree)
        self.assertIn("def h", reduced.to_source())
        self.assertEqual(reducer.applied_edits, [])

    def test_falls_back_to_a_single_edit(self):
        # Only the dict may be collapsed; the list must keep its elements.
        source = "a = {'k': 1}\nb = [1, 2, 3]\nprint(a, b)\n"
        tree = self.parse(source)
        reducer = DataTypeSimplificationReducer(self.grammar)
        reduced = reducer.reduce(tree, requires("[ 1 , 2 , 3 ]"))
        text = reduced.to_source()
        self.assertIn("{ }", text)
        self.assertIn("[ 1 , 2 , 3 ]", text)
        self.assertGreater(reducer.tests_used, 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(reducer.applied_edits), 1)

    def test_single_edit_fallback_can_be_switched_off(self):
        source = "a = {'k': 1}\nb = [1, 2, 3]\nprint(a, b)\n"
        tree = self.parse(source)
        reducer = DataTypeSimplificationReducer(self.grammar,
                                               try_single_edits=False)
        reduced = reducer.reduce(tree, requires("[ 1 , 2 , 3 ]"))
        self.assertIs(reduced, tree)
        self.assertEqual(reducer.tests_used, 1)

    def test_no_opportunity_costs_no_test(self):
        tree = self.parse("print(1)\n")
        reducer = LoopUnrollingReducer(self.grammar)
        reduced = reducer.reduce(tree, always())
        self.assertIs(reduced, tree)
        self.assertEqual(reducer.tests_used, 0)
        self.assertFalse(reducer.last_response.changed)

    def test_budget_bounds_the_tests(self):
        source = "a = {'k': 1}\nb = [1, 2, 3]\nprint(a, b)\n"
        tree = self.parse(source)
        reducer = DataTypeSimplificationReducer(self.grammar, max_tests=1)
        reducer.reduce(tree, never())
        self.assertEqual(reducer.tests_used, 1)

    def test_every_concrete_reducer_reports_its_transformation(self):
        pairs = [
            (FunctionInliningReducer, FUNCTION_INLINING),
            (LoopUnrollingReducer, LOOP_UNROLLING),
            (VariableEliminationReducer, VARIABLE_ELIMINATION),
            (DataTypeEliminationReducer, DATA_TYPE_ELIMINATION),
            (DataTypeSimplificationReducer, DATA_TYPE_SIMPLIFICATION),
        ]
        for cls, kind in pairs:
            self.assertEqual(cls(self.grammar).transformation, kind)

    def test_empty_tree_is_left_alone(self):
        tree = self.parse("")
        reducer = FunctionInliningReducer(self.grammar)
        self.assertIs(reducer.reduce(tree, always()), tree)
